originalTitle: Britain’s Georgia Hunter Bell surges to emphatic 1500m European gold
summary: Georgia Hunter Bell raced clear on the final lap to win the women’s 1500m in 4:07.78sec, with Klaudia Kazimierska in second and Patricia Silva third
content: Georgia Hunter Bell’s glorious summer continues to take her to fresh summits. The 32-year-old was simply sublime as she demolished a decent European 1500m field to add another title to her swelling collection. It proved to be the final gold British medal of these championships, as Britain agonisingly missed out on coming top of the medal table to Italy by the slimmest margins. First Jazmin Sawyers failed to win long jump gold by a centimetre to Larissa Iapichino of Italy. Then, in the final race of the championships, Italy’s Lorenzo Benati held off Britain’s Charlie Dobson by 0.03sec in the men’s 4x400m relay. It meant that Italy finished top with 10 gold medals, one ahead of the British team, but it still marked an excellent effort on a thrilling final day. Hunter Bell led from the front. As expected, the women’s 1500m turned into a slow and tactical race. But in the last lap burn up, Hunter Bell truly ignited. Her 58.44sec final 400m took her 10 metres clear as she crossed the line in 4:07.78. No wonder when she crossed the line she applauded herself for a job well done. “That last 150m is always my favourite part of the race, and it was really nice to come down the home stretch and know that I had it,” said Hunter Bell, who finished a second clear of Poland’s Klaudia Kazimierska, with Portugal’s Patricia Silva taking a surprise bronze. Over the past five months, Hunter Bell has won world indoor 1500m gold, 800m Commonwealth Games gold, and the European title. She now believes she can add a fourth to her collection at the Ultimate Championships in Budapest next month. Soon afterwards Sawyers jumped an outdoor long jump personal best of 6.99m to win silver against a high-quality field. It was all the more impressive given that she sustained a serious achilles injury 18 months ago. But she fell tantalising short of Iapichino, who jumped seven metres. France’s Hilary Kpatcha finished with a leap of 6.98m. Two more silvers for Britain quickly followed in the women’s and men’s 4x400m as Britain finished with 19 medals. As seven days of action in Birmingham came to an end with Mondo Duplantis taking pole vault gold in 6.15m, Jack Buckner, the chief executive of UK Athletics, hailed the European Championships as a huge success. Buckner said that he was particularly pleased that Friday night’s epic 800m final starring Keely Hodgkinson, Audrey Werro and Femke Broeders-Bol had attracted around four million viewers on BBC One as he insisted his sport had cut through into the mainstream. “Everyone is absolutely delighted with the BBC numbers,” he said. “I heard it was 3.8m but that was without iPlayer. So they’ve been talking over four million on Friday night, which is really strong. So we are absolutely delighted and everyone is buzzing. “This is a big sport that cuts through with big stars and that’s what we want. We want big heroes and big names doing amazing things.” “Another star emerged here in Amy Hunt, which is fantastic for the sport,” he added. “Keely, in the way she conducts herself and the way she handles herself, is a role model. And then you look at all of them in the 4x100m relays and you just go ‘that’s what we want this country to be’. Buckner also hinted that Britain was tempted to bid again in the near future, with the rebuilt stadium at Crystal Palace a potential option. “It’s been absolutely fantastic,” he said. “We loved doing it. We learn a lot. We think we could do it better and we’re going to do it again.” Buckner also defended the struggles with ticket sales at the start of the week – and said that UKA had sold nearly three-quarters of all tickets in the 23,000-capacity Alexander Stadium. “In the buildup we did work with schools and we did work with community groups, and overall we’ve sold 73% of the tickets,” he said. “In any other country in the world, if they’ve delivered that result in ticketing, they’d have been jumping up and down with excitement. But our expectations are higher and we’re OK with that. We’ve sold out the last four days so it’s been a world-class ticketing result, but we want better.”
chineseTitle: 英国选手 Georgia Hunter Bell 夺得 1500m 欧洲金牌
chineseSummary: 乔治娅·亨特·贝尔 (Georgia Hunter Bell) 在最后一圈以 4 分 07.78 秒的成绩赢得女子 1500 米比赛，克劳迪娅·卡齐米尔斯卡 (Klaudia Kazimierska) 获得第二名，帕特里夏·席尔瓦 (Patricia Silva) 获得第三名
chineseContent: 乔治亚·亨特·贝尔 (Georgia Hunter Bell) 辉煌的夏天继续带领她登上新的巅峰。这位 32 岁的选手简直太棒了，她摧毁了欧洲 1500 米赛场，为她不断增加的收藏再添一个冠军头衔。事实证明，这是英国在本届锦标赛上获得的最后一枚金牌，英国队以微弱优势与奖牌榜榜首的意大利队失之交臂。首先，贾兹明·索耶斯（Jazmin Sawyers）以一厘米之差输给了意大利选手拉里萨·亚皮奇诺（Larissa Iapichino），未能赢得跳远金牌。随后，在锦标赛的最后一场比赛中，意大利选手洛伦佐·贝纳蒂 (Lorenzo Benati) 在男子 4x400 米接力比赛中以 0.03 秒的优势领先英国选手查理·多布森 (Charlie Dobson)。这意味着意大利队以 10 枚金牌名列榜首，领先英国队一枚，但这仍然标志着在激动人心的最后一天的出色表现。亨特·贝尔（Hunter Bell）在前线领先。正如预期的那样，女子 1500 米比赛变成了一场缓慢而富有策略性的比赛。但在最后一圈燃尽时，亨特·贝尔真正点燃了。最后 400m 跑用时 58.44 秒，她以 4 分 07.78 秒冲线，领先 10 米。难怪当她越过界限时，她为自己做得很好而鼓掌。 “最后 150m 始终是比赛中我最喜欢的部分，能够冲过最后冲刺阶段并知道我已经做到了，真是太好了，”亨特·贝尔 (Hunter Bell) 说道，他以第二名的成绩领先波兰选手克劳迪娅·卡齐米尔斯卡 (Klaudia Kazimierska)，而葡萄牙选手帕特里夏·席尔瓦 (Patricia Silva) 意外获得了铜牌。在过去的五个月里，亨特·贝尔赢得了世界室内1500米金牌、英联邦运动会800米金牌以及欧洲冠军头衔。她现在相信她可以在下个月布达佩斯举行的终极锦标赛上为她的收藏添加第四个。不久之后，索耶斯在高素质的参赛队伍中跳出户外跳远个人最好成绩6.99m，获得银牌。考虑到她跟腱严重受伤，这更令人印象深刻 18
